Threshold of a decision rule for a given false selection probability

Source: R/CalibrateThreshold.R
CalibrateThreshold.Rd

Finds, from the results of SimSelection under a scenario in which no cohort should be selected over the reference cohort (for example cohorts that are all identical), the smallest threshold for which the proportion of simulated trials that select a cohort other than the reference is at most alpha. Decision rules based on different statistics can then be compared at the same false selection probability.

Usage

CalibrateThreshold(
  results,
  statistic = c("br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "ntb_lower", "wr", "wo"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  admissibility = TRUE
)

Arguments

results

Data frame returned by SimSelection.

statistic

One of "br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "ntb_lower", "wr" and "wo".

alpha

Target probability of selecting a cohort other than the reference.

admissibility

Logical: use the admissibility of the benefit-risk scores ("br_diff" and "br_ref" only).

Value

A data frame with columns statistic, alpha, threshold and p_nonreference (the achieved proportion of trials that select a cohort other than the reference).

Details

The decision rules are those of SelectionOC: a cohort other than the reference is selected when the largest statistic among the candidate cohorts exceeds the threshold. With statistic = "br_diff" and admissibility = TRUE, trials in which the reference cohort is not admissible and another cohort is admissible select that cohort whatever the threshold; when their proportion exceeds alpha, no threshold achieves alpha and the result is NA with a warning. The threshold is one of the simulated values of the statistic (or -Inf when no trial needs to be excluded), and the achieved proportion can be smaller than alpha because of ties and the finite number of trials.

See also

SelectionOC, SimSelection

Examples

set.seed(1)
res <- data.frame(sim = rep(1:500, each = 3), group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 500),
                  is_reference = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), 500))
res$ntb <- ifelse(res$is_reference, NA, rnorm(1500, 0, 0.1))
res$wr <- ifelse(res$is_reference, NA, exp(rnorm(1500, 0, 0.3)))
CalibrateThreshold(res, "ntb", alpha = 0.1)
#>   statistic alpha threshold p_nonreference
#> 1       ntb   0.1  0.164408            0.1
CalibrateThreshold(res, "wr", alpha = 0.1)
#>   statistic alpha threshold p_nonreference
#> 1        wr   0.1   1.67811            0.1
